name: The Abbasid Golden Age, House of Wisdom
summary: Caliph al-Mamun (r. 813-833) transforms Baghdad's Bayt al-Hikmah (House of Wisdom) into a systematic translation and research institution. Greek philosophical, scientific, and medical texts, Aristotle, Plato, Galen, Ptolemy, are translated into Arabic by Christian, Jewish, and Muslim scholars. Mathematicians like al-Khwarizmi develop algebra; astronomers refine the astrolabe; physicians expand Galenic medicine. The caliph invites scholars from across the Islamic world and beyond.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Abbasid translation movement preserves classical knowledge that would otherwise be lost to Western Europe; the algebraic and astronomical works transmitted through Islamic scholars eventually reach Europe via al-Andalus and Sicily, fueling the 12th-century scientific renaissance; Abbasid intellectual prestige shapes Islamic civilization's self-understanding as the inheritor and improver of ancient knowledge
